detail.title: Foundational Synthesis: Self-Verification and Methodological Falsification
detail.summary: We synthesized research on error detection mechanisms and observer disagreement. By mapping DeepSeekMath-V2's approach to self-verifiable mathematical reasoning against Karl Popper's methodology of scientific research programmes, we identified that both autonomous verification and falsification frameworks serve to refine inferential models against observational data. These notebooks formalize the distinction between observational discrepancy and systematic inferential error.

detail.title: Self-Verification as Error Detection
detail.summary: This notebook explores how internal self-verification processes, as seen in DeepSeekMath-V2, allow for the identification of inferential errors independent of external ground truth.
detail.reason: Synthesis of self-verification benchmarks with falsification theory supports the project's goal of distinguishing between observational data and inferential error.

detail.title: Methodological Roots of Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: Analysis of observer disagreement through the lens of Popper's methodology suggests that disparate conclusions often stem from incompatible 'hard cores' of assumed theory rather than observational error.
detail.reason: Existing evidence allows provisional synthesis to address the project's inquiry into observer disagreement.
